question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; bounded first-principles reassessment of public plugin/extension access
trigger: User challenges the completed editor.plugin() to editor.extension() migration, asks for the originating plan, and requests harsh honest review of Plate plugins as product compositions above Plite extensions. Review and history recording only.
requirements: Explain the actual originating plan and recorded rationale; distinguish installed ownership from the public consumer vocabulary.
Keep Plite extensions independently usable and preserve Plate plugin product state, schema presentation, configuration and React policy.
Retain one canonical installed identity/registry and existing execution groups; no duplicate runtime owner or compatibility alias.
Preserve inferred descriptor capabilities, nominal ancestry and rejection, raw adoption, optional presence, candidate publication, exact-view binding and stale-access handling.
Assess this one disputed contract without reopening unrelated Plate features or executing a repair.
evidenceReuse: Supersedes the September 12 plate-api recommendation only where one installed registry was taken to require one public accessor. The originating plan, design-contract alternatives and design-decisions log were read. Current types, dispatch and product/raw consumers were rechecked because the earlier review fingerprint is stale after adoption. Historical production identity/transaction results remain unchanged and are not rerun or treated as evidence for naming. One bounded read-only worker independently traced current dispatch and consumer differences; the lead verified decisive references.
summary: Pursue restoring editor.plugin(Plugin) as the Plate product contract while retaining editor.extension(Extension) for raw extension access and the shared Plite installed owner. The September 12 plan explicitly rejected separate public portals because plugin projections include core capabilities; current source still has distinct descriptor domains, result types and a nominal dispatch into createPluginPortal. Inclusion of substrate capabilities does not eliminate the product consumer job. Preserve the registry/ancestry improvements and direct transaction groups; avoid a second installation system or two equivalent plugin spellings. Next owner: Task design plan for the exact descriptor boundary and adoption.
alternatives: Keep one overloaded extension: defensible as a generic installed-capability lookup, but it hides a real product/substrate distinction that remains in constructor vocabulary, result types and dispatch; fewer public verbs do not remove those concepts.

Restore product plugin access and retain raw extension access over one registry: strongest direction; align authoring/installation and consumer domains while reusing identity, execution, product projection and stores.
Add plugin as an unrestricted compatibility alias: reject; no need for two equivalent spellings of the same plugin projection. Specify distinct descriptor domains instead.
Delete Plate plugin authoring or move its fields into Plite: reject; product configuration, stores, schema presentation and React policy have independent current jobs.
Rebuild separate plugin installation maps or tx.plugin: reject; no current product job requires another installed owner or per-transaction enumeration.
Rename all plugins to extensions or add a generic capability abstraction: reject; neither removes the product compiler/contract nor demonstrates a material consumer or runtime benefit.
proofLimits: Bounded source/plan/consumer/assertion review only. No tests, typechecks, browser or performance experiments were rerun. Existing production receipts measure identity/ancestry and transaction-map deletion, not the public spelling on an otherwise identical registry. Shared installation and direct transactions remain; proposed plugin access is unimplemented. Preserve historical implementation/proof state separately from this revised target. Future adoption must prove exact inference, raw adoption, optional lookup, nominal ancestry, candidate and view lifecycle, store/API identity and teaching parity. Any additional runtime machinery requires its own matched evidence.
